title: Trung Kien · 13/11 · Craft and Structure, Information and Ideas +2

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sarah Hinckley et al.’s 2009 study of planktonic ecosystems used a nutrient-phytoplankton-zooplankton (NPZ) model.
• Diane Stoecker et al. (2017): NPZ models rely “on the differentiation of the planktonic communities into phytoplankton or zooplankton functional types,” excluding mixotrophic plankton.
• Phytoplankton are exclusively phototrophic, producing nutrients via photosynthesis.
• Zooplankton are exclusively phagotrophic, obtaining nutrients by consuming other organisms.
• Mixotrophic plankton are capable of both phototrophic and phagotrophic.
• Stoecker et al.: “Mixotrophy changes the basic trophic structure of…ecosystems; most of the unicellular organisms at the base of the plankton food web can no longer be regarded as strictly producers or consumers.”

The student wants to challenge the model used in Hinckley et al.’s study. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Since it classifies plankton as exclusively phototrophic producers or phagotrophic consumers, the model used in Hinckley et al.’s study may misrepresent planktonic ecosystems, in which—as Stoecker et al. note—many plankton combine these functions.
options.B: Hinckley et al.’s 2009 study used an NPZ model, which, as Stoecker et al. point out, unnecessarily categorizes organisms as either phytoplankton, zooplankton, or mixotrophic plankton.
options.C: By restricting plankton functional types to phytoplankton and zooplankton, the model used in Hinckley et al.’s study of planktonic ecosystems overlooks the many mixotrophic species that—as Stoecker et al. note—function as neither producers nor consumers.
options.D: Hinckley et al.’s model disregards the respective roles of producers and consumers—organisms that, as Stoecker et al. emphasize, are essential to the trophic structure of the plankton food web.

questions.stem:
Anthropologist, activist, and musician Lila Downs draws on a variety of Mexican musical genres in her 2023 album La Sánchez. __________ she draws on corridos, rancheras, and other genres of northern Mexico, even though she is from the southern Mexican city of Oaxaca. "La Sánchez is my contribution," Downs says in an interview, "as a southern woman, that also considers this music as hers."

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

options.A: Specifically,
options.B: Therefore,
options.C: In conclusion,
options.D: Rather,

questions.stem:
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

Can artificial intelligence (AI) truly capture human consciousness? Louisa Hall’s novel Speak pursues this inquiry by weaving together five stories across different centuries, from a Puritan woman’s diary to an AI’s confessions. These narratives reveal unexpected connections, suggesting that our drive to preserve human expression through technology stems from fear that without such mediation, our voices might be lost to time. Hall ultimately posits that AI represents not merely a technological achievement but the latest manifestation of an existential attempt to transcend mortality.

options.A: It presents a provocative paradox, summarizes how a novel questions the assumptions underlying the paradox, and reframes the author’s message as an argument about AI and human mortality.
options.B: It poses a philosophical dilemma, outlines five storylines that explore this dilemma across different time periods, and reveals how these stories converge to challenge conventional views about technology.
options.C: It begins with a question about the role of AI in society, explains how an author seeks to answer that question in a novel, and proposes that preserving human expression is more important than technological advancement.
options.D: It introduces a novel’s central question, describes how the author employs a specific narrative structure to investigate that question, and presents the author’s conclusion about a broader human concern.

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• 1950s: The Institute of African Studies (IAS) is proposed and initially formed at the University College of the Gold Coast (now the University of Ghana).
• Some faculty, including Peter Shinnie and his committee, support a linguistic and cultural focus for the IAS.
• This approach to African Studies is aligned with the British colonial academic models that were imposed prior to Ghana's independence in 1957.
• Other faculty resist this narrow scope, calling instead for an interdisciplinary approach that includes African history, economics, and politics.
• Early 1960s: Ghana's president Kwame Nkrumah reorganizes the IAS under an interdisciplinary, African-centered vision.
• Nkrumah's reforms are part of a broader post-1945 movement to challenge colonial systems in Africa.

The student wants to place Kwame Nkrumah's reorganization of the IAS in historical context.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Nkrumah's early 1960s reorganization of the IAS was built directly on British academic models that had long supported interdisciplinary African Studies in Ghanaian universities.
options.B: Following Ghana's 1957 independence, Nkrumah reorganized the IAS with a linguistic and cultural focus, as recommended by Peter Shinnie and his committee.
options.C: Nkrumah reorganized the IAS in the early 1960s to reflect an interdisciplinary, African-centered vision, aligning with a broader post-1945 movement to challenge colonial systems in Africa.
options.D: Nkrumah's changes to African Studies reflected faculty concerns that the field should move beyond colonial frameworks and include areas like history, politics, and economics.

questions.stem:
While some biologists cite the general lineage species concept (Queiroz 1998), others adhere to the biological species concept (Coyne and Orr 2004), with at least fourteen other concepts used across the field. Such lack of consensus, however, isn't necessarily cause for alarm. Scholars supporting a pluralist approach—in place of a single, monistic concept—to defining a species __________ that a diversity of species concepts fits their equally diverse applications throughout the discipline.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.A: is arguing
options.B: to argue
options.C: argue
options.D: argues

questions.stem:
Many artists associated with hyperpop, a movement in electronic music that emerged in the 2010s, conform to the model perfected by the American duo 100 gecs: bold synthesizer arrangements, propulsive beats, and electronically manipulated vocals. Yet the movement is hardly uniform: British recording artist Charli XCX incorporates pop melodies into the hyperpop sound, for example. Such stylistic diversity is encouraged in part by the music-streaming app Spotify, whose curated playlist of hyperpop songs balances cohesion with variety.

Which statement about Charli XCX is best supported by the text?

options.A: Her inclusion on Spotify's hyperpop playlist inspired established artists to embrace stylistic experimentation.
options.B: She developed her unique sound without being influenced by other artists on Spotify's hyperpop playlist.
options.C: While some of her recordings conform to the model perfected by 100 gecs, others reject it outright.
options.D: Her music diverges from the typical hyperpop sound but doesn't abandon it.

questions.stem:
The following text is from Charles Chesnutt's 1905 novel The Colonel's Dream. Mr. Morton and Mr. Hale work together.

Mr. Morton, the senior partner, who sat opposite Hale, was an older man—a safe guess would have placed him somewhere in the debatable ground between forty and fifty; of a good height, as could be seen even from the seated figure, the upper part of which was held erect with the unconscious ease which one associates with military training. As used in the text, what does the word “good” most nearly mean?

options.A: Considerable
options.B: Well-behaved
options.C: Reliable
options.D: Talented

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

Tlaxcoapan is a municipality in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico. Municipalities are governmental regions responsible for providing many public services to their residents. One service they provide is street lighting. Tlaxcoapan's population was 28,626 in 2020. Its population was 26,758 in 2010. Hidalgo is divided into 84 municipalities.

The student wants to emphasize the 2020 population of Tlaxcoapan. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: As a municipality in Hidalgo, Tlaxcoapan is responsible for providing public services to its population.
options.B: In 2020, the municipality of Tlaxcoapan had a population of 28,626.
options.C: As of 2020, Tlaxcoapan was one of 84 municipalities in Hidalgo, Mexico.
options.D: Home to 26,758 people, the governmental region was responsible for providing street lighting to its population in 2010.

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The farm-size transition hypothesis predicts that economic pressures associated with modernization result in smaller farms amalgamating into larger-scale commercial farms.
• Masters et al. (2013): The average farm size in Asia "already has or will soon begin to rise."
• Promkhambut et al. (2023) argue that small rice farms in Thailand have adopted modern farming methods without a significant scaling-up of farm size.
• Promkhambut et al.: "The persistence of [small] rice farms [in Thailand] does not represent a 'failure' to modernize...or a 'truncated' transition—it is a response to modernization."

The student wants to make and support a claim regarding the applicability of the farm-size transition hypothesis to Thailand. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Masters et al. report that the average farm size "already has or will soon begin to rise" in Asia, a finding that is consistent with the farm-size transition hypothesis.
options.B: The predicted shift to large-scale commercial farming may not hold true for rice farms in Thailand, where, according to Promkhambut et al., rice farms have remained small as they've modernized.
options.C: Taken together, the studies by Masters et al. and Promkhambut et al. suggest that rice farms in Thailand have responded to the economic pressures associated with modernization by expanding in size.
options.D: Although the farm-size transition hypothesis may be applicable to some countries in Asia, it is inconsistent with the development of rice farming in Thailand.

questions.stem:
The interiors of many temples in the ancient Middle East needed to satisfy a precise set of acoustic demands: the sounds of chants and hymns should travel with clarity, while profound silences should be fully felt and appreciated. In a research paper, a student claims that the users of one such temple were aware of how the materials that were used within the structure could affect sound quality and that they deliberately applied this knowledge to influence how sound was experienced in the space.

Which quotation from a work by a historian would most directly support the student's claim?

options.A: "The acoustic environment of the temple was best suited for music that eschewed ornamentation in favor of simple melodies, harmonies, and rhythms."
options.B: "Many researchers believe that the central chamber of the temple had a high ceiling, a feature that has since become essential to the acoustic design of modern concert halls."
options.C: "During special occasions, curtains were placed inside the temple to minimize reverberation and confine the sound to designated locations."
options.D: "The innermost room of the temple was likely among the quietest spaces in the interior of the temple."

questions.stem:
Claudine Mukesharugo, a tea producer in Rwanda, and Vinicio Gonzales, a coffee grower in Guatemala, are both part of a global community of small farmers who partner with the grassroots organization Thrive Farmers. Their partnership with the organization is based on a revenue-sharing model that puts the farmers at the forefront. With this model, farmers aren't just supplying initial crops but are stakeholders through the sale of the finished products.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.A: To explain that some small farmers follow a business model that allows them to have greater involvement in the sale of products made with their crops
options.B: To describe how a partnership between two farms that produce different types of crops led to the development of a new business model for small farmers
options.C: To introduce the idea that around the world, small farmers have increasingly been managing their farms as if they were large businesses
options.D: To suggest that the Thrive Farmers organization is generating greater global demand for crops grown by small farmers

questions.stem:
While many initiatives aimed at limiting atmospheric warming focus on curbing emissions of methane (CH4), a greenhouse gas that is typically generated by microbially mediated processes, Lisa Y. Stein and Mary E. Lidstrom caution that under certain circumstances, such efforts cause microbial communities to accelerate production of nitrous oxide (N2O), another potent greenhouse gas, thus offsetting the impact of CH4 reduction. Researchers, therefore, need to take such biological interactions into account to ensure that any CH4 mitigation strategy has an overall positive climate effect.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.A: It mentions a phenomenon that negatively affects the environment, summarizes competing methods for remedying that phenomenon, and then concedes that even apparently distinct methods share similar problems.
options.B: It describes a widely accepted approach to addressing an environmental issue caused by a type of chemical emissions, indicates a potential disadvantage of that approach, and then discusses an implication of that disadvantage.
options.C: It reports on a predicament resulting from emissions of a particular greenhouse gas, outlines a strategy aimed at solving that predicament, and then admonishes those who utilize that strategy without fully comprehending its ramifications.
options.D: It presents an ongoing environmental challenge, demonstrates why the impact of that challenge may intensify over time, and then criticizes a misguidedly narrow attempt to address that impact.

questions.stem:
Text 1
Coal mining and other human activities are significant sources of atmospheric methane (CH4), but, as Sander Houweling and colleagues have shown, so too are naturally occurring emissions, such as those from wild animals. This biogenic CH4 is challenging to monitor given natural sources' variability and spatial diffusion, but one promising approach is to use CH4 flux data from extant monitoring infrastructure as proxies for CH4 fluxes in unmonitored areas.

Text 2
Sparkle Malone and colleagues examined the United States' network of eddy covariance (EC) towers—the equipment used to track CH4 fluxes—to evaluate the utility of network data for quantifying biogenic CH4 Malone et al. found that EC towers are disproportionately concentrated in areas where biogenic CH4 emissions are known to be elevated, a pattern that seriously compromises the representativeness of network data.

Based on the texts, Malone et al. (Text 2) would most likely agree with which statement about the "approach" described in Text 1?

options.A: It could compromise the accuracy of the biogenic CH4 emissions data that EC towers collect in areas with elevated emissions.
options.B: It would only be viable if the EC towers monitoring biogenic CH4 emissions could detect smaller fluxes than they can at present.
options.C: It may suggest that biogenic CH4 emissions in unmonitored areas are higher than they actually are.
options.D: It is likely to be useful for determining biogenic CH4 emissions in unmonitored areas of some regions but not of most regions.

questions.stem:
A typical string quartet consists of two violin players, a viola player, and a cello player. When a string quartet performs, one violinist and the cellist usually sit facing the audience. The violist and the other violinist usually sit facing each other. This seating arrangement causes the viola’s carved sound openings, or f-holes, to be angled away from the audience. Therefore, if the viola player has a musical solo and wants to make sure that the audience can hear it clearly, the violist typically __________

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: looks at the sheet music instead of looking at the audience.
options.B: instructs the other members of the quartet to play louder.
options.C: plays at the same volume as the cellist.
options.D: shifts position in order to face outwards toward the audience.

questions.stem:
Psychologists Gregory Bryant, Dorsa Amir, and colleagues investigated cross-cultural perceptions of spontaneous (real) laughter and volitional (fake or forced) laughter. Study participants from 21 societies, including those in Japan and Turkey, listened to randomized recordings of 18 spontaneous laughs taken from natural conversations between pairs of women and 18 volitional laughs produced separately by 18 different women in response to an instruction to laugh. Analysis of the participants' evaluations of the laughs prompted the team to conclude that the ability to distinguish between spontaneous and volitional laughter appears to be universal across cultures.

Which potential finding from another study, if true, would most directly strengthen the team's conclusion?

options.A: Listeners from both Japan and Turkey tend to be able to determine how well two people know each other based on recordings of their conversation.
options.B: Spontaneous laughter typically has a recognizably higher pitch than volitional laughter, regardless of what society the speakers in a conversation are from.
options.C: There is some evidence of correlation between the average size of communities in a society and judgments of spontaneous and volitional laughter by listeners in that society.
options.D: Acoustic features of spontaneous laughter, such as pitch and intensity, have measurable variations both within and across societies.

options.A: they have increased in value.
options.B: have they increased in value?
options.C: they have increased in value?
options.D: have they increased in value.

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Physicist Lise Meitner was a key collaborator with chemist Otto Hahn in Berlin for over three decades.
• In 1938, forced to flee Nazi Germany due to her Jewish heritage, Meitner relocated to Stockholm, Sweden.
• In December 1938, Hahn observed unexpected barium when bombarding uranium with neutrons but could not explain the result.
• Working in Sweden with her nephew Otto Frisch, Meitner calculated the energy released and provided the first theoretical explanation for nuclear fission in 1939.
• In 1944, Otto Hahn was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery, while Meitner's indispensable theoretical contribution was overlooked by the committee.

The student wants to contextualize Lise Meitner's theoretical breakthrough in nuclear fission.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Although Otto Hahn observed barium during neutron experiments in 1938, he won the 1944 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of nuclear fission.
options.B: After collaborating with Otto Hahn in Berlin for three decades, physicist Lise Meitner was forced to flee Germany for Sweden in 1938.
options.C: While in exile in Sweden in 1939, Meitner provided the crucial theoretical explanation and energy calculations for the unexplained nuclear fission observations reported by Hahn.
options.D: Lise Meitner and her nephew Otto Frisch conducted research in Stockholm, Sweden, after Meitner left Berlin in 1938.
